long_biography.plain_text:
Aristrain was prepared for the family metals business from a young age and took charge after his father died in 1986. The inherited group made beams and other industrial products. Under his leadership, its assets were ultimately sold to Aceralia, while the Aristrain group and José María received shares in the buyer. Those shares later became interests in Arcelor and then ArcelorMittal through successive combinations.

He now acts principally through investment holdings rather than as an executive manufacturer. He retains an ArcelorMittal interest, while Corporación Aristrain is Tubacex's largest shareholder and filings trace the holding indirectly to him. A 2026 voting agreement increased the holding company's board influence but expressly excluded joint control or involvement in industrial management. Company stakes, merger values and transaction prices belong to the relevant corporations or deals; they are not equivalent to Aristrain's personal cash or net worth. His fortune is therefore inherited in origin but materially shaped by his management, exchange of operating assets for quoted shares and later industrial investments.
